title: Nine Pounds in a Drawer
subtitle: 账单与票据 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 账单与票据（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：账单与票据（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：bill　|　正文 329 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bill 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 my father was handed ① a bill for nine pounds and said the handing was the whole of the insult. The ② bill, meaning the paper and not the debt, was kept in a drawer for eleven years and was paid in March by somebody else; a bill, he said, is the only object that is more dangerous folded than open.

Every ③ bill in that house was opened by my mother, and the ④ bill from the doctor, meaning the one for the winter visits and not either of those, was the only one she ever hid. A bill, my grandmother said, is nine parts arithmetic and one part a hand that shakes; my father said the arithmetic is the part you can argue with.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ bill was the whole of the bird, meaning the beak and not the paper. The ⑥ bill, meaning the horny mouth and not any of that, is the only part of an animal that is used for both fighting and eating; a bill, he said, is either something you owe or the only word that means both an invoice and a beak. She said the beak came first.

By 1964 the ⑦ bill had become a line in a ledger, and the ledger had become an argument about the date. The ⑧ bill of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine pounds and eleven years in a drawer; a bill, she said, is either the paper from the doctor or the reason you learned to open your own post. He said the opening was the part that mattered.

The ⑨ bill I remember is the one from the doctor, which was paid in 1967 and never mentioned. A ⑩ bill, my grandmother said in 1969, is the only paper that improves by being kept; every bill, she said, is a beak that has agreed to look like an invoice. She said the beak was never the cruel part.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 账单（指那张纸，与债务相对）
C. 固定搭配：be handed a bill 收到／被递给一张账单
D. n. 账单（指屋里每一张）
E. n. 账单（指医生那一张）
G. n. 喙（抽象：那只角质的嘴）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The bill, meaning the paper and not the debt
bill was the whole of the bird
The bill, meaning the horny mouth
the bill had become a line in a ledger
The bill of the whole thing
A bill, my grandmother said in 1969

answers.why: be handed a bill 意为“收到／被递给一张账单”，1949 年有人递给父亲一张九镑的账单。
bill 意为“账单”，指那张纸而不是债务，它在抽屉里放了十一年，三月由别人付掉了。
bill 指屋里每一张账单，那屋里每一张都是母亲拆的。
bill 指医生那一张（冬天出诊的那一张），是唯一她藏起来的。
bill 意为“鸟喙、喙”，指那只角质的嘴，叔叔说 bill 就是那只鸟的全部。
bill 为抽象用法，指那只角质的嘴，是一个动物身上唯一既能打架又能吃饭的部分。
bill 意为“账单”，到 1964 年这个 bill 成了账簿里的一行。
bill 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九镑和在抽屉里放的十一年。
bill 意为“账单”，我记得的是医生那一张，1967 年被付掉，从此再没提起过。
bill 为抽象总称，祖母说账单是唯一会因为被留着而变好的纸。

items: 1949 年有人递给父亲一张九镑的账单，他说递这个动作才是侮辱的全部。（be handed a bill）
那张账单，指的是那张纸而不是债务，在抽屉里放了十一年，三月由别人付掉了。（bill）
那屋里每一张账单都是母亲拆的。（bill）
医生那张账单，指的是冬天出诊的那一张，是唯一她藏起来的。（bill）
叔叔说 bill 就是那只鸟的全部，指的是喙而不是那张纸。（bill）
1969 年祖母说，账单是唯一会因为被留着而变好的纸。（bill）

The bill, meaning the paper and not the debt, was kept in a drawer for eleven years and was paid in March by somebody else.
Every bill in that house was opened by my mother.
The bill from the doctor, meaning the one for the winter visits and not either of those, was the only one she ever hid.
My uncle said bill was the whole of the bird, meaning the beak and not the paper.
A bill, my grandmother said in 1969, is the only paper that improves by being kept.
